To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we can learn a mapping from input audio waveforms to 3D facial animations with a deep neural network, (2) we can disentangle the variations in facial expressions into a compact latent code, (3) we can use the latent code as an intuitive control of emotional state, and (4) we achieve real time performance and low latency.

we propose a novel approach to audio-driven facial animation that learns a compact, latent representation of the emotion of the speaker, and that we evaluate this approach on a dataset of 10,000 videos of real people.

(i) we propose a novel end-to-end deep neural network architecture for audio-driven facial animation, and (ii) we demonstrate that our method is able to learn a compact, latent space that disambiguating the variations in facial expressions that cannot be explained from the audio alone.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the joint end-to-end training of a deep neural network for pose and emotion is a powerful approach for learning the mapping from audio to 3D facial animations, and that this approach can be used for real-time applications.
